claim: p53 induced the transcription of miR-139-5p
source: p53 induced the transcription of miR-139-5p, which in turn suppressed the protein levels of phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D), an oncogenic protein involved in multiple tumor promoting processes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1 and 2, including miRNA sequencing, qRT-PCR, ChIP assays, and luciferase reporter assays demonstrating p53-dependent induction of miR-139-5p.

claim: miR-139-5p suppressed the protein levels of phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D)
source: p53 induced the transcription of miR-139-5p, which in turn suppressed the protein levels of phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D), an oncogenic protein involved in multiple tumor promoting processes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing Western blot analysis and luciferase reporter assays demonstrating that miR-139-5p directly targets and reduces PDE4D protein levels.

claim: PDE4D is an oncogenic protein involved in multiple tumor promoting processes
source: p53 induced the transcription of miR-139-5p, which in turn suppressed the protein levels of phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D), an oncogenic protein involved in multiple tumor promoting processes.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous literature (Lin et al., 2013; Ogawa et al., 2002; Pullamsetti et al., 2013; Rahrmann et al., 2009) describing PDE4D's oncogenic properties.

claim: Knockdown of p53 reversed the effects of p53 on miR-139-5p and PDE4D
source: Knockdown of p53 reversed these effects.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 1E showing that p53 knockdown decreased miR-139-5p expression.

claim: Overexpression of miR-139-5p decreased PDE4D levels
source: Also, overexpression of miR-139-5p decreased PDE4D levels and increased cellular cAMP levels, leading to BIM-mediated cell growth arrest.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 3B showing Western blot analysis of PDE4D after miR-139-5p mimic transfection.

claim: Overexpression of miR-139-5p increased cellular cAMP levels
source: Also, overexpression of miR-139-5p decreased PDE4D levels and increased cellular cAMP levels, leading to BIM-mediated cell growth arrest.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 4A showing cAMP measurement after miR-139-5p mimic transfection.

claim: Overexpression of miR-139-5p led to BIM-mediated cell growth arrest
source: Also, overexpression of miR-139-5p decreased PDE4D levels and increased cellular cAMP levels, leading to BIM-mediated cell growth arrest.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 4C and 4D showing BIM induction and cell growth arrest that is rescued by BIM knockdown.

claim: There is a significant inverse correlation between the expression of miR-139-5p and that of PDE4D in human colorectal tumor specimens
source: Furthermore, our analysis of human colorectal tumor specimens revealed significant inverse correlation between the expression of miR-139-5p and that of PDE4D.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5A showing qRT-PCR analysis and Pearson's correlation analysis of 50 paired human colon tumor specimens.

claim: Overexpression of miR-139-5p suppressed the growth of xenograft tumors
source: Finally, overexpression of miR-139-5p suppressed the growth of xenograft tumors, accompanied by decrease in PDE4D and increase in BIM.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5B showing tumor volume measurements in xenograft models.

claim: Overexpression of miR-139-5p in xenograft tumors was accompanied by decrease in PDE4D
source: Finally, overexpression of miR-139-5p suppressed the growth of xenograft tumors, accompanied by decrease in PDE4D and increase in BIM.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5D showing immunohistochemistry analysis of PDE4D in xenograft tumors.

claim: Overexpression of miR-139-5p in xenograft tumors was accompanied by increase in BIM
source: Finally, overexpression of miR-139-5p suppressed the growth of xenograft tumors, accompanied by decrease in PDE4D and increase in BIM.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 5E showing Western blot analysis of BIM in xenograft tumors.

claim: p53 inactivates oncogenic PDE4D by inducing the expression of miR-139-5p
source: These results demonstrate that p53 inactivates oncogenic PDE4D by inducing the expression of miR-139-5p.
evidence: The claim is supported by the collective experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing the p53-miR-139-5p-PDE4D pathway.

claim: Abnormal regulation of miRNAs is associated with human cancer development and staging
source: Abnormal regulation of miRNAs is associated with human cancer development and staging (Lu et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lu et al., 2005.

claim: A number of miRNAs have been identified as p53 target genes
source: Over the past decade, increasing attention has been drawn to the role of miRNAs in p53 signaling network, and a number of miRNAs have been identified as p53 target genes (Liao et al., 2014a).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Liao et al., 2014a.

claim: p53 target miRNAs are involved in multiple biological processes, including cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, glycolysis
source: These miRNAs are involved in multiple biological processes, including cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, glycolysis and so on.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about p53 target miRNAs.

claim: p53 target miRNAs often connect p53 with other signaling pathways
source: Also, they often connect p53 with other signaling pathways (Christoffersen et al., 2010; Sachdeva et al., 2009; Liang et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Christoffersen et al., 2010; Sachdeva et al., 2009; Liang et al., 2013.

claim: miRNAs have been appreciated as important mediators of p53's tumor suppression functions
source: Although miRNAs have been appreciated as important mediators of p53's tumor suppression functions, a lot still remain unexplored to better understand the fine-tuning of p53 signaling and crosstalk with other pathways by these RNAs.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about miRNAs and p53.

claim: miR-139-5p is a novel p53 target gene
source: In this study, we identified miR-139-5p as a novel p53 target gene and demonstrated a new pathway connecting p53 and miR-139-5p with an oncogenic protein PDE4D as a new target of this miRNA and its downstream cAMP signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figures 1 and 2 showing p53-dependent induction of miR-139-5p.

claim: PDE4D is a new target of miR-139-5p
source: In this study, we identified miR-139-5p as a novel p53 target gene and demonstrated a new pathway connecting p53 and miR-139-5p with an oncogenic protein PDE4D as a new target of this miRNA and its downstream cAMP signaling.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing direct targeting of PDE4D by miR-139-5p.

claim: HCT116 p53-/- cells were genetically engineered to lose the expression of wild type (WT) p53
source: In order to identify potential p53 target microRNAs, we used colon cancer cell lines, HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/-, the latter of which were genetically engineered to lose the expression of wild type (WT) p53 (Bunz et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Bunz et al., 1998.

claim: Inauhzin-C (INZ-C) is a p53 activating compound
source: Both cells were treated with 4 μM Inauhzin-C (INZ-C), which is a p53 activating compound discovered in our lab (Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2012.

claim: miR-34a, miR-1246 and miR-143 are known p53 target microRNAs
source: The results revealed that in addition to known p53 target microRNAs, such as miR-34a, miR-1246 and miR-143 (Liao et al., 2014a; Suzuki et al., 2009), miR-139 was also significantly induced in HCT116 p53+/+, but not HCT116 p53-/-, cells, suggesting miR-139 as a potential p53 target (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Liao et al., 2014a; Suzuki et al., 2009.

claim: miR-139 was significantly induced in HCT116 p53+/+, but not HCT116 p53-/-, cells after INZ-C treatment
source: The results revealed that in addition to known p53 target microRNAs, such as miR-34a, miR-1246 and miR-143 (Liao et al., 2014a; Suzuki et al., 2009), miR-139 was also significantly induced in HCT116 p53+/+, but not HCT116 p53-/-, cells, suggesting miR-139 as a potential p53 target (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by miRNA sequencing data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: miR-139-5p was significantly induced only in p53 positive, but not in p53 null, cells after INZ-C treatment
source: We independently confirmed this observation by detecting miR-139-5p expression after treating HCT116 p53+/+/HCT116 p53-/- and H460 (WT p53)/H1299 (p53 null) cells with DMSO or 4 μM INZ-C. miR-139-5p was significantly induced only in p53 positive, but not in p53 null, cells (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: p53 knockdown decreased miR-139-5p expression by more than 50% in H460 and U2OS cells
source: In contrast, p53 knockdown decreased miR-139-5p expression by more than 50% in H460 and U2OS cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: miR-139-5p is a possible p53 target gene
source: These data indicate that miR-139-5p is a possible p53 target gene.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing p53-dependent regulation of miR-139-5p.

claim: There is a highly conserved putative p53 responsive element (RE) located at the 5' flanking region of the miR-139 gene
source: After carefully analyzing the genomic sequence of the miR-139 gene using p53MH algorism (Hoh et al., 2002), we found a highly conserved putative p53 responsive element (RE) located at the 5' flanking region (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic analysis using p53MH algorithm and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The binding of p53 with the p53RE in the miR-139 promoter was dramatically increased upon Doxorubicin treatment in H460 and HCT116 p53+/+ cells
source: In both cell lines, the binding of p53 with the p53RE was dramatically increased upon Doxorubicin treatment as compared to non-treatment control, indicated by p53RE sequence pulled down with p53 specific antibody DO-1, but not non-specific immunoglobulin G (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: GFP-p53 markedly induced luciferase activity in a dose-dependent manner when wild type miR-139 p53RE, but not the mutant p53RE, was used
source: Also, we assessed luciferase expression driven by either a wild type or a mutant-p53RE-motif-containing miR-139 sequence (Figure 2C) in H1299 cells. GFP-p53 markedly induced luciferase activity in a dose-dependent manner when wild type miR-139 p53RE, but not the mutant p53RE, was used (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: p53 binds to the miR-139 promoter region and thus regulates the transcription of miR-139
source: These results clearly show that p53 binds to the miR-139 promoter region and thus regulates the transcription of miR-139.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the ChIP and luciferase reporter assay data.

claim: The 3'-untranslated region (3'-UTR) of PDE4D contains miR-139-5p targeting sequence
source: By using the online microRNA target prediction tool (Maragkakis et al., 2009), we searched for potential RNA targets of miR-139-5p. After screening several candidates, PDE4D turned out to be an ideal target as its 3'-untranslated region (3'-UTR) contains miR-139-5p targeting sequence (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by bioinformatic prediction and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Overexpression of miR-139-5p mimic markedly reduced the expression of PDE4D in H460 and A549 cells
source: Overexpression of miR-139-5p mimic markedly reduced the expression of PDE4D in H460 and A549 cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: IGF-IR is a previously reported miR-139-5p target
source: The type-I insulin-like growth factor receptor (IGF-IR), a previously reported miR-139-5p target (Shen et al., 2012), was also decreased by miR-139-5p mimic, indicating the activity of miR-139-5p used here (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Shen et al., 2012 and Western blot data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: PDE4D belongs to the family of phosphodiesterases and is a cyclic AMP (cAMP) specific phosphodiesterase with several splice variants
source: PDE4D belongs to the family of phosphodiesterases and is a cyclic AMP (cAMP) specific phosphodiesterase with several splice variants (Omori and Kotera, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Omori and Kotera, 2007.

claim: PDE4D is an oncogenic protein that regulates cancer cell proliferation, angiogenesis and apoptosis
source: It is an oncogenic protein that regulates cancer cell proliferation, angiogenesis and apoptosis (Lin et al., 2013; Ogawa et al., 2002; Pullamsetti et al., 2013; Rahrmann et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2013; Ogawa et al., 2002; Pullamsetti et al., 2013; Rahrmann et al., 2009.

claim: miR-139-5p regulates PDE4D expression by directly binding to the target sequence at 3'-UTR of PDE4D mRNA
source: When co-transfecting H1299 cells with miR-139-5p, only the pMIR-PDE4D-WT, but not the pMIR-PDE4D-mutant, displayed suppressed expression (Figure 3D), suggesting that miR-139-5p regulates PDE4D expression by directly binding to the target sequence at 3'-UTR of PDE4D mRNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Activation of p53 by doxorubicin in H460 and A549 cells significantly reduced the protein levels of PDE4D
source: In line with the above results, activation of p53 by doxorubicin in H460 and A549 cells significantly reduced the protein levels of PDE4D (Figure 3E, left panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3E, left panel.

claim: PDE4D variants with smaller molecular weight have been reported to possess stronger oncogenic activities due to the lack of functional inhibitory domains as compared to the longer forms
source: Notably, the PDE4D variants with smaller molecular weight have been reported to possess stronger oncogenic activities due to the lack of functional inhibitory domains as compared to the longer forms (Lin et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2013.

claim: miR-139-5p transfection and doxorubicin treatment led to similar expression inhibition of both the long and the short variants of PDE4D
source: Nevertheless, miR-139-5p transfection and doxorubicin treatment led to similar expression inhibition of both the long and the short variants of PDE4D, indicating that this newly identified pathway has broader inhibition on PDE4D.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the Western blot data showing both PDE4D variants are reduced.

claim: Knocking down p53 elevated PDE4D expression in H460 and A549 cells
source: In contrast, knocking down p53 elevated PDE4D expression in these two cell lines (Figure 3E, right panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3E, right panel.

claim: miR-139-5p mimic reduced PDE4D in PC-3, a p53 null cell line
source: We then assessed the effect of miR-139-5p on PDE4D in PC-3, a p53 null cell line, and found similar reduction of PDE4D by miR-139-5p mimic (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Nutlin-3 disrupts MDM2-p53 interaction and therefore activates p53
source: To further validate the regulatory role of p53 on PDE4D, we also treated HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/- cells with 10 μM Nutlin-3 (Nut), which disrupts MDM2-p53 interaction and therefore activates p53 (Vassilev et al., 2004), and 5 nM Actinomycin D (ActD), which causes ribosomal stress-mediated p53 activation (Iapalucci-Espinoza and Franze-Fernández, 1979), and found PDE4D was reduced by both of these two drugs only in p53 positive, but not p53 negative, cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Vassilev et al., 2004.

claim: Actinomycin D causes ribosomal stress-mediated p53 activation
source: To further validate the regulatory role of p53 on PDE4D, we also treated HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/- cells with 10 μM Nutlin-3 (Nut), which disrupts MDM2-p53 interaction and therefore activates p53 (Vassilev et al., 2004), and 5 nM Actinomycin D (ActD), which causes ribosomal stress-mediated p53 activation (Iapalucci-Espinoza and Franze-Fernández, 1979), and found PDE4D was reduced by both of these two drugs only in p53 positive, but not p53 negative, cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Iapalucci-Espinoza and Franze-Fernández, 1979.

claim: PDE4D was reduced by Nutlin-3 and Actinomycin D only in p53 positive, but not p53 negative, cells
source: To further validate the regulatory role of p53 on PDE4D, we also treated HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/- cells with 10 μM Nutlin-3 (Nut), which disrupts MDM2-p53 interaction and therefore activates p53 (Vassilev et al., 2004), and 5 nM Actinomycin D (ActD), which causes ribosomal stress-mediated p53 activation (Iapalucci-Espinoza and Franze-Fernández, 1979), and found PDE4D was reduced by both of these two drugs only in p53 positive, but not p53 negative, cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The suppression of PDE4D is p53 dependent in response to various stresses
source: These results suggest that this suppression of PDE4D is p53 dependent in response to various stresses.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing p53-dependent PDE4D suppression by multiple p53 activators.

claim: Doxorubicin inhibited pMIR-PDE4D activity, but introduction of miR-139-5p inhibitor reversed this inhibition
source: Furthermore, doxorubicin inhibited pMIR-PDE4D activity, but introduction of miR-139-5p inhibitor reversed this inhibition (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The suppression of PDE4D protein by doxorubicin was compromised in the presence of miR-139-5p inhibitor
source: Consistently, the suppression of PDE4D protein by doxorubicin was also compromised in the presence of miR-139-5p inhibitor (Figure 3G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Activation of p53 can induce the expression of miR-139-5p that in turn suppresses the expression of oncogenic protein PDE4D
source: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that activation of p53 can induce the expression of miR-139-5p that in turn suppresses the expression of oncogenic protein PDE4D.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental data showing the p53-miR-139-5p-PDE4D pathway.

claim: PDE4D is a cAMP specific phosphodiesterase
source: Since PDE4D is a cAMP specific phosphodiesterase, ectopic expression of miR-139-5p in A549 cells led to significant increase of cellular cAMP levels (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about PDE4D function.

claim: Ectopic expression of miR-139-5p in A549 cells led to significant increase of cellular cAMP levels
source: Since PDE4D is a cAMP specific phosphodiesterase, ectopic expression of miR-139-5p in A549 cells led to significant increase of cellular cAMP levels (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by cAMP measurement data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Doxorubicin treatment increased cellular cAMP levels in A549 cells, which were alleviated by the miR-139-5p inhibitor
source: Also, consistent with our results shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3G, doxorubicin treatment increased cellular cAMP levels in A549 cells, which were alleviated by the miR-139-5p inhibitor (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cAMP measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nutlin-3 increased cellular cAMP levels in A549 cells, which was reversed in the presence of miR-139-5p inhibitor
source: In addition, Nutlin-3, a more specific p53-activating reagent, showed similar effect on cAMP level, which was also reversed in the presence of miR-139-5p inhibitor (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by cAMP measurement data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In H1299 cells, which are p53-null and express non-detectable PDE4D, neither doxorubicin nor miR-139-5p affected cellular cAMP level
source: In contrast, in H1299 cells, which are p53-null and express non-detectable PDE4D, neither doxorubicin nor miR-139-5p affected cellular cAMP level (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cAMP measurement data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The rescue effect of miR-139-5p on A549 cell growth inhibition by Nutlin-3 was correlated with the change of cAMP levels
source: Notably, the rescue effect of miR-139-5p on A549 cell growth inhibition by Nutlin-3 was correlated with the change of cAMP levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by MTT assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: p53 activation could modulate cAMP levels through miR-139-5p
source: These data indicate that p53 activation could modulate cAMP levels through miR-139-5p.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing p53-dependent cAMP modulation via miR-139-5p.

claim: Depletion of PDE4D was previously reported to induce BIM-mediated apoptosis through activation of the cAMP pathway
source: Depletion of PDE4D was previously reported to induce BIM-mediated apoptosis through activation of the cAMP pathway (Lin et al., 2013; Zambon et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2013; Zambon et al., 2011.

claim: Introduction of miR-139-5p into H460 and A549 cells dramatically increased BIM protein expression
source: We found that introduction of miR-139-5p into H460 and A549 cells dramatically increased BIM protein expression (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Treatment with 10 μM Nutlin-3 induced BIM expression in HCT116 p53+/+, but not HCT116 p53-/-, cells
source: As expected, treatment with 10 μM Nutlin-3 also induced BIM expression in HCT116 p53+/+, but not HCT116 p53-/-, cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), supporting that BIM induction is p53-dependent.
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: BIM induction is p53-dependent
source: As expected, treatment with 10 μM Nutlin-3 also induced BIM expression in HCT116 p53+/+, but not HCT116 p53-/-, cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 4), supporting that BIM induction is p53-dependent.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing BIM induction only in p53-positive cells.

claim: A549 cell growth was significantly inhibited by miR-139-5p or Nutlin-3, both of which were attenuated by knocking down BIM using siRNA
source: Consequently, A549 cell growth was significantly inhibited by miR-139-5p or Nutlin-3, both of which were attenuated by knocking down BIM using siRNA (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by MTT assay data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Introduction of miR-139-5p inhibitor into A549 cells significantly alleviated cell growth inhibition by several p53 activating drugs, including INZ-C, Actinomycin D and Nutlin-3
source: Inversely, introduction of miR-139-5p inhibitor into A549 cells significantly alleviated cell growth inhibition by several p53 activating drugs, including INZ-C, Actinomycin D and Nutlin-3 (Figure 4—figure supplements 3 and 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by MTT assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 3 and 6.

claim: In response to p53 activation, increased miR-139-5p induces BIM-mediated cell growth arrest via the PDE4D/cAMP pathway
source: These results demonstrate that in response to p53 activation, increased miR-139-5p induces BIM-mediated cell growth arrest via the PDE4D/cAMP pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental data showing the pathway from p53 to cell growth arrest.

claim: miR-139-5p expression was significantly lower in colon tumor specimens than in their adjacent normal tissues
source: In order to determine the clinical relevance of miR-139-5p regulation of PDE4D, we obtained 50 paired human colon tumor specimens and their adjacent normal tissues and conducted qRT-PCR analysis on these specimens. miR-139-5p expression was significantly lower while PDE4D was higher in these tumor specimens than that in their normal tissues (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from 50 paired human colon tumor specimens shown in Figure 5A.

claim: PDE4D expression was higher in colon tumor specimens than in their adjacent normal tissues
source: In order to determine the clinical relevance of miR-139-5p regulation of PDE4D, we obtained 50 paired human colon tumor specimens and their adjacent normal tissues and conducted qRT-PCR analysis on these specimens. miR-139-5p expression was significantly lower while PDE4D was higher in these tumor specimens than that in their normal tissues (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data from 50 paired human colon tumor specimens shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Pearson's correlation analysis revealed that miR-139-5p is inversely correlated with PDE4D expression in colon tumor specimens and normal tissues
source: Pearson's correlation analysis of the expression results from the tumor specimens and normal tissues revealed that miR-139-5p is inversely correlated with PDE4D expression (Figure 5A, bottom panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pearson's correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A, bottom panel.

claim: Clinical data provide evidence supporting miR-139-5p as a negative regulator of PDE4D
source: These results provide clinical evidence supporting miR-139-5p as a negative regulator of PDE4D, consistent with our above results.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the clinical correlation data.

claim: SW480 xenograft tumors stably overexpressing miR-139-5p grew significantly slowly as compared to control tumors starting at day 16 after inoculation
source: To validate this clinical correlation, we established a xenograft model using SW480 cells stably expressing either scramble oligos (Control) or miR-139-5p. As expected, miR-139-5p expressing tumors grew significantly slowly as compared to control tumors starting at day 16 after inoculation (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by tumor volume measurements shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The difference of miR-139-5p expression in xenograft tumors was comparable to that observed in human specimens
source: The difference of miR-139-5p expression in these two groups of tumors was comparable to that observed in human specimens (Figure 5C vs Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5C compared to Figure 5A.

claim: In the miR-139-5p overexpressing tumors, PDE4D expression was markedly repressed
source: Immunohistochemistry analysis revealed that in the miR-139-5p overexpressing tumors, PDE4D expression was markedly repressed, while tumor cell proliferation was significantly inhibited as reflected by Ki67 staining (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the miR-139-5p overexpressing tumors, tumor cell proliferation was significantly inhibited as reflected by Ki67 staining
source: Immunohistochemistry analysis revealed that in the miR-139-5p overexpressing tumors, PDE4D expression was markedly repressed, while tumor cell proliferation was significantly inhibited as reflected by Ki67 staining (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: BIM expression was elevated in miR-139-5p overexpressing xenograft tumors
source: Consistent with our in vitro observation, BIM expression was also elevated in miR-139-5p tumors (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The tumor suppressor role of miR-139-5p is likely attributed to its regulation of the PDE4D/BIM pathway
source: These findings suggest that the tumor suppressor role of miR-139-5p is likely attributed to its regulation of the PDE4D/BIM pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the xenograft data showing tumor suppression correlated with PDE4D/BIM pathway changes.

claim: This study for the first time demonstrates that p53 can induce the expression of miR-139-5p
source: In summary, this study for the first time demonstrates that p53 can induce the expression of miR-139-5p (Figure 1 and Figure 2), which in turn suppresses the expression of an oncogenic protein PDE4D (Figure 3) and leads to cAMP/BIM-mediated cell growth arrest (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by the collective experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: miR-139 was previously shown to be downregulated in human hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer
source: As a potential tumor suppressor, miR-139 was previously shown to be downregulated in human hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer with characterized targets including Rho-kinase 2, IGF-IR and RAP1B (Guo et al., 2012; Shen et al., 2012; Wong et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Guo et al., 2012; Shen et al., 2012; Wong et al., 2011.

claim: Rho-kinase 2, IGF-IR and RAP1B are characterized targets of miR-139
source: As a potential tumor suppressor, miR-139 was previously shown to be downregulated in human hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer with characterized targets including Rho-kinase 2, IGF-IR and RAP1B (Guo et al., 2012; Shen et al., 2012; Wong et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Guo et al., 2012; Shen et al., 2012; Wong et al., 2011.

claim: PDE4D is an oncogenic protein that is upregulated in various human cancers
source: Here, we identified PDE4D, an oncogenic protein that is upregulated in various human cancers (Lin et al., 2013), as another novel target of this miRNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Lin et al., 2013.

claim: Inhibition or depletion of PDE4D significantly induces apoptosis and inhibits proliferation of cancer cells
source: Inhibition or depletion of PDE4D significantly induces apoptosis and inhibits proliferation of cancer cells (Lin et al., 2013; Ogawa et al., 2002; Rahrmann et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2013; Ogawa et al., 2002; Rahrmann et al., 2009.

claim: The oncogenic property of PDE4D involves the cAMP/BIM pathway
source: Notably, the oncogenic property of PDE4D involves the cAMP/BIM pathway (Lin et al., 2013; Zambon et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2013; Zambon et al., 2011.

claim: cAMP is an important secondary messenger mediating diverse cellular processes with protein kinase A as its main effector
source: cAMP is an important secondary messenger mediating diverse cellular processes with protein kinase A as its main effector (Taskén and Aandahl, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Taskén and Aandahl, 2004.

claim: Lower cAMP levels favor cancer cell survival and proliferation
source: In particular, lower cAMP levels favor cancer cell survival and proliferation, which can be reversed by inhibition of PDE4D, the cAMP specific phopsphodiesterase (Goldhoff et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2013; Murata et al., 2000; Ogawa et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Goldhoff et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2013; Murata et al., 2000; Ogawa et al., 2002.

claim: Lower cAMP levels favoring cancer cell survival and proliferation can be reversed by inhibition of PDE4D
source: In particular, lower cAMP levels favor cancer cell survival and proliferation, which can be reversed by inhibition of PDE4D, the cAMP specific phopsphodiesterase (Goldhoff et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2013; Murata et al., 2000; Ogawa et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Goldhoff et al., 2008; Lin et al., 2013; Murata et al., 2000; Ogawa et al., 2002.

claim: The tumor suppressor role of p53 is highly attributable to its regulation of target genes involved in cell cycle arrest, apoptosis and senescence
source: The tumor suppressor role of p53 has been extensively documented over the last two decades, and is highly attributable to its regulation of target genes involved in cell cycle arrest, apoptosis and senescence (Bieging et al., 2014; Levine, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bieging et al., 2014; Levine, 2011.

claim: p53 is a critical mediator of metabolic pathways that are important for tumor survival
source: More recent discoveries revealed that p53 is also a critical mediator of metabolic pathways that are important for tumor survival (Bieging et al., 2014; Jiang et al., 2015; Wang and Gu, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bieging et al., 2014; Jiang et al., 2015; Wang and Gu, 2014.

claim: p53 can modulate cellular cAMP levels by inhibiting PDE4D expression via miR-139-5p
source: Based on our findings, we propose a p53-miR-139-5p-PDE4D-cAMP-BIM pathway as a novel pathway that can mediate p53's tumor suppression function to modulate cellular cAMP levels by inhibiting PDE4D expression via miR-139-5p, and deregulation of this pathway would be highly associated with tumorigenesis (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the collective experimental data and proposed as a model in Figure 5F.

claim: Deregulation of the p53-miR-139-5p-PDE4D-cAMP-BIM pathway would be highly associated with tumorigenesis
source: Based on our findings, we propose a p53-miR-139-5p-PDE4D-cAMP-BIM pathway as a novel pathway that can mediate p53's tumor suppression function to modulate cellular cAMP levels by inhibiting PDE4D expression via miR-139-5p, and deregulation of this pathway would be highly associated with tumorigenesis (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is speculative, inferred from the experimental data and proposed as a hypothesis.

claim: HCT116 p53+/+ and HCT116 p53-/- cells were generous gifts from Dr. Bert Vogelstein at the John Hopkins Medical Institutes
source: Human HCT116 p53+/+ (RRID: CVCL_0291) and HCT116 p53-/- (RRID: CVCL_S744) cells were generous gifts from Dr. Bert Vogelstein at the John Hopkins Medical Institutes.
evidence: The claim is a statement of fact about the source of cell lines.

source: A549 (RRID: CVCL_0023), HepG2 (RRID: CVCL_0027), U2OS (RRID: CVCL_0042), H460 (RRID: CVCL_0459) and H1299 (RRID: CVCL_0060) cells were purchased from American Type Culture Collection (ATCC).
evidence: The claim is a statement of fact about the source of cell lines.

claim: PC3 cells were purchased from ATCC
source: All cells were cultured in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM) and PC3 (RRID: CVCL_0035) cells (also from ATCC) in RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, 50 U/ml penicillin and 0.1 mg/ml streptomycin at 37°C in 5% CO2.
evidence: The claim is a statement of fact about the source of cell lines.

source: Fifty paired colorectal tumors and adjacent non-tumor tissues were collected and histopathologically diagnosed at the Departments of Gastrointestinal Surgery and Pathology, the First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University.
